question: During CuT 380A insertion using the withdrawal technique, at which anatomical landmark should you release the device from the inserter?

answers.text: At the level of the internal cervical os

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Releasing at the internal os leads to low placement in the uterine cavity, which is the most common cause of early expulsion. The device must be advanced to the fundus.

answers.text: At the uterine fundus, confirmed by gentle resistance and fundal depth on the inserter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The inserter should be advanced until gentle fundal resistance is felt, then the plunger is withdrawn while holding the inserter steady ('withdrawal technique'), releasing the device at the fundus. Fundal placement is the single most important factor preventing early expulsion.

answers.text: After the inserter tip has passed the external cervical os by 2 cm

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 2 cm past the external os is still within the endocervical canal in most women, not the fundus. Premature release in the canal virtually guarantees expulsion or malposition.

answers.text: When the woman reports a sensation of pressure, regardless of inserter depth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Patient-reported pressure is not a reliable indicator of fundal placement. The clinician must use the uterine sound depth measurement to guide placement to the fundus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the CuT 380A insertion technique. The most critical step is fundal placement — the inserter must reach the fundus before the device is released. Premature release is the leading cause of early expulsion.

Excellent. Fundal placement is the cornerstone of successful IUCD insertion. Sound the uterus first to determine cavity depth, advance the inserter to the fundus, then withdraw the tube while keeping the plunger stationary.
